answer: Six years of weekly columns under one name. Content creation history turns that archive into the gate: articles published under one byline for six years. The writing lives on other people's servers, dated and searchable, so the cedar of the forgery is the archive itself - a farm cannot print six years of back issues overnight. Each fake needs its own hundred articles, and the echo inside each is an editor who remembers the author and readers who read the work. The cipher that seals it is the deadline: no machine writes a six-year column habit in a weekend.
